distractors.reason: 'Depend' is never followed by 'of' in this sense. 'Of' is used after nouns such as 'picture of' or 'mother of'.
We do not use 'from' after 'depend'. Even when the source is a thing, the structure is 'depend on'.
'In' follows verbs such as 'believe in' or 'interested in', not 'depend'.

example_sentence: The success of my project will depend ___ the quality of my data.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes suelen traducir 'depender de' literalmente y decir 'depend of'. En inglés, el verbo 'depend' siempre va seguido de 'on'.
explanation: In English, 'depend' takes the preposition 'on' to introduce what something relies on. This is a fixed verb-preposition pair, so the preposition cannot be chosen freely.

related_collocations.example: You can rely on my data.
My project focuses on renewable energy.
The report consists of five sections.

memory_tip: DEPEND ON = something relies on something else (depend on the data, depend on the results) | the preposition is fixed, so learn the pair together
